_comment: Prompts of the new HypoDeduce phases, written by us (the paper gives no prompts). 'inherit' reuses a SoapFL prompt unchanged, so method selection and scoring are identical to the SoapFL baseline and only the multi-hypothesis control flow differs. In the SoapFL prompts the 'Possible Causes' placeholder is filled with ONE hypothesis at a time.

phase_prompt: One or more tests in the test suite "{test_suite}" failed due to a single bug.
According to the test code, error stack trace and test output of each failed test, and the behaviors of the failed tests listed below:

As the {assistant_role}, you will reason abductively: propose {num_hypotheses} DIFFERENT hypotheses, each describing a distinct possible defect in the production code that could explain ALL of these test failures. The hypotheses must not be rewordings of each other; together they should cover the plausible root causes. Order them from the most to the least likely.

Only consider defects in the production code, NOT in the test code. For each hypothesis, state what is wrong, where in the production code it is probably located, and which observation (stack trace, assertion message or test output) supports it.
Use exactly this format, one hypothesis per entry:
Hypothesis 1: <description of the first possible defect>
Hypothesis 2: <description of the second possible defect>
One or more tests in the test class "{test_suite}" failed due to a single bug.
According to the test code, error stack trace and test output of each failed test, the hypothesis about the root cause, and the classes that are covered by all of the failed tests listed below:

As the {assistant_role}, assume that the hypothesis is true and recommend the {num_classes} covered classes that are most likely to contain the defect it describes, ordered from the most to the least suspicious. You must ONLY select classes from the Covered Classes List.
You should NOT select the test class "{test_suite}", since the root cause exists in the production code.
Write the full name of every recommended class between pound signs, one class per line, for example:
(no model call: hypothesis selection and ranking are computed from the method scores)
